Noah Kahan Sets Stadium World Tour For 2027
Noah Kahan will trek across the great divide and around the world next year.
The singer-songwriter on Thursday revealed plans for a two-month world tour of stadiums dubbed “The Last of the Bugs” that will run April 24-July 25. The jaunt will launch with a show in Athens, Georgia, and wraps with three concerts at London’s Wembley Stadium. See the full itinerary below.

The 31-date tour will hit North American cities first, including four nights at Fenway Park in Boston. After a June 18 show at Metlife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ, it will head to Europe on July 1, including a pair of shows at Aviva Stadium in Dublin. The Dublin, London and some other European shows were announced previously.
There are no Southern California concerts on the slate for now, with the closest being mid-May stops in Las Vegas and San Francisco. But there are some open dates before and after those shows. Watch on Deadline
Vermont native Kahan is hot off his latest album The Great Divide, which topped charts in the U.S., UK and many other countries after its April release. A later deluxe version of the disc was dubbed The Great Divide: The Last of the Bugs . His latest track is “Draw You Out,” written for The Hunger Games: Sunrise of the Reaping and released last month. It serves as the l ead single for the soundtrack album to the film that hits theaters on November 20.
Kahan sang a moving version of Simon & Garfunkel’s “Bridge Over Troubled Water” for the “In Memoriam” segment at the Emmys in September. That came weeks after he called out Donald Trump for the use of the singer’s “American Cars” in a White House social media post.
